card.summary: Free open-source (GPL) self-hosted repository server; no quota because there is no vendor. 'Pulp is an open source project that makes it easy for developers ...

free_tier.stated: Free open-source (GPL) self-hosted repository server; no quota because there is no vendor. 'Pulp is an open source project that makes it easy for developers to fetch, upload, organize and distribute Software Packages on-prem or in the cloud.'

egress.terms: Free by construction. Self-hosted; you pay (or don't) for your own bandwidth.

record.interface_detail: rest (pulpcore REST API), plus repository endpoints for rpm/deb/python/container/generic; also ships OCI images of itself
record.tooling: pulpcore REST API + `pulp-cli`, plus `podman`/`docker` for the container deploy and standard package clients against published repos. Documented at pulpproject.org/pulpcore/docs/. It is also the backend Fedora COPR uses, which is a working-scale endorsement.
record.chaining: Same self-hosted arithmetic: unlimited instances × your disk. Notably it is the engine under COPR's Pulp backend, so its per-repo retention setting (`retain_package_versions`) is the lever that makes 'unlimited' repos actually behave like storage.
record.limits_note: No vendor limits. Operationally: you must run Postgres + object storage + workers; 'unlimited' means 'as much disk as you attach'. No built-in public/anonymous CDN.
record.reliability_note: Very reliable (Red Hat-backed, used by COPR); the cost is operational complexity, not data loss.

evidence.proved: read live: 'Pulp is an open source project that makes it easy for developers to fetch, upload, organize and distribute Software Packages on-prem or in the cloud'
read live: COPR uses a 'Pulp backend', and Pulp's `retain_package_versions` repository setting controls retention — evidence Pulp runs at Fedora scale
